scope: Forge, Git serving, decentralized collaboration and WASM CI/workflow donors for glopyglerky/gitr; part of a multi-track survey.
method: Primary repository metadata, pinned manifests/licenses/source modules, fork parents and compare endpoints, official project/crate documentation. No upstream builds, benchmarks or tests executed.
gitr_constraints: Retain current redb durability/publication authority unless separately justified.
Retain selected Wasmi execution runtime; translate foreign workflow plans into gitr durable jobs.
User permits evaluating a lawful license change. Apache/copyleft candidates are conditional rather than excluded; inherited third-party restrictions remain.

candidates.description: Blazing fast, self hosted Git hosting in Rust. One binary, no external services.
candidates.reuse: Vendoring or depending on crates/rbit-workflow wholesale is the strongest immediate CI option: budgeted YAML, expression/filter semantics, triggers, cron, matrix planning, job specifications and runner protocol types.
candidates.limitations: Full forge uses SQLite and system Git transport. Adapt plans to existing gitr durable jobs, receipts and Wasmi; runner behavior and trust/authentication still need independent integration.

candidates.description: IronForge — Lightweight self-hosted Git hosting platform written in Rust
candidates.reuse: Native gix-based upload/receive-pack, HTTP/SSH forge, MCP models, package registries, runner and CI isolation interfaces.
candidates.limitations: Current receive-pack updates refs sequentially with PreviousValue::Any and does not advertise atomic. Replace publication with gitr fenced CAS transaction. Full product includes SQL and web frontend Node build.

candidates.description: Lightweight, open-source, self-hosted Git server and forge written in Rust. Gitea/Forgejo/GitHub alternative with pull requests, CI/CD and built-in MCP for AI agents.
candidates.reuse: Documented IronForge derivative, formerly ForgeKeep; native rg-git plus forge/core, mirrors, package registry, CI matrix and MCP surfaces.
candidates.limitations: AGPL derivative is eligible only with a compatible lawful distribution/service licensing design. Its NOTICE preserves upstream MIT provenance. Do not infer all fork modules have been audited for atomic publication.

candidates.description: Programmable git infrastructure on top of object storage. Think turbopuffer for git. Open source alternative to Pierre (code.storage) and Cloudflare Artifacts.
candidates.reuse: Replicated repository ledger, immutable read snapshots, optimistic ref publication, resumable cold-layer object access, Git v2 serving and direct commit API.
candidates.limitations: Custom ledger/storage architecture is not a redb drop-in. Raft/raft-engine, lsm-tree, allocator and crypto native dependencies require profile review. Benchmark/Jepsen claims not reproduced.

candidates.description: Programmable git infrastructure on top of object storage. Think turbopuffer for git. Open source alternative to Pierre (code.storage) and Cloudflare Artifacts.
candidates.reuse: Verified upstream fork; commit d29138ad3a8806effc7bbe72ddf6a1ad214401cc adds wait-for-done advertisement and push.negotiate regression test.
candidates.limitations: One unique commit and one upstream commit behind at compared snapshots; use patch/test, not the entire older fork.

candidates.description: A git server built on object storage and optimized for high throughput.
candidates.reuse: Smart Git protocol parsing, pack validation/promotion and CAS status reporting around a trait-based server with gix.
candidates.limitations: SlateDB and object store are its selected backend; adapt storage contract to redb. Product auth, PRs and branch protection explicitly out of scope.

candidates.description: A self-hostable Git server for agent-scale traffic: packs in object storage, per-branch history in Postgres. Pre-alpha.
candidates.reuse: aspen-proto/aspen-pack plus metadata contracts for versioned refs, push CAS, pack closure, commit-index fallback and job enqueue; interop/fuzz/chaos fixtures.
candidates.limitations: Explicitly pre-alpha with unmet launch gates; full system PostgreSQL/SQLite. Distinct from brittonr/aspen. Retain gitr DB and publication authority.

candidates.description: Mega2: second-generation, Git-compatible monorepo engine built for AI agents. Trunk-based Git storage and hosting in Rust (Postgres + S3-compatible object storage), with optional Agent Session Capture, Git LFS, build artifacts, and an OCI registry.
candidates.reuse: Ceres pack ingest and publication paths, Jupiter object storage, LFS/OCI/artifact storage, trace/agent-capture models and audit surfaces.
candidates.limitations: Public edition is trunk/storage-oriented without full Change List UI and multibranch monorepo product. PostgreSQL, OpenSSL/libvault, libc/native allocators; dependency licenses remain separate.

candidates.description: Mega is an open-source implementation of Google Piper — a Git-compatible monorepo engine built for the AI Agent era.
candidates.reuse: Historical Mega forge and layout lineage; compare only if functionality absent from Mega2 is needed.
candidates.limitations: Archived; primary language TypeScript. Prefer current Mega2 for engine investigation.

candidates.description: Rust-based Software development platform (forge) with built-in vcs, issue tracking and code review
candidates.reuse: gitarena-issues crate provides Rust git-bug issue operations, identity/issue merge and snapshots; forge routes/data model are useful references.
candidates.limitations: Issue README documents lost updates with external writers and nontransactional Git/SQL writes. Full forge mixes gix and libgit2 and uses PostgreSQL. Keep redb CAS authority.

candidates.description: 🏯 blazingly fast web frontend for git repositories
candidates.reuse: Small Git web browse/search interface and gix rendering/read-side examples.
candidates.limitations: RocksDB native C++, tree-sitter grammars and system git http-backend. It is not a new Git engine or complete forge.

candidates.license_assessment: MIT declared; rewrite provenance to inspect
candidates.description: A headless git forge with a simple web interface. A self-hosted alternative to github written in Rust.
candidates.reuse: SSH/headless forge administration, authentication and repo-management patterns; accompanying TypeScript rgit-web exists.
candidates.limitations: README calls it rewrite of archived GPL2 MoriGM/rgit. src/git.rs runs system Git; MIT declaration does not by itself prove no inherited GPL code. Not native Git engine.

candidates.description: GitHub-style browser for rgit (rabun-git) repositories.
candidates.reuse: Companion frontend for Rabun Git.
candidates.limitations: TypeScript; low priority for a Rust engine.

candidates.reuse: Historical ancestry to inspect before adopting rconnelly/rgit.
candidates.limitations: Archived, obsolete ancestor; no selected source transplantation recommended.

candidates.description: A hyper-hyperfast web frontend for git repositories written in Rust.
candidates.reuse: Small gix/maud/smol web viewer with zlib-rs.
candidates.limitations: A viewer, not forge authority. Tree-sitter C and optional jemalloc; source-level feature audit still needed.

candidates.description: cgit rewritten in Rust — drop-in CGI replacement
candidates.reuse: cgit-style CGI frontend and read-side object/rendering glue.
candidates.limitations: gix plus vendored Lua via mlua; metadata/UI donor rather than Git engine.

candidates.license_assessment: MIT declaration in Cargo; license file absent
candidates.description: Lightweight self-hosted Git service with a Rust backend, Flutter Web UI, SQLite, Git LFS, SSH/HTTP Git support, and GitLab-compatible storage migration.  轻量级自托管 Git 服务，采用 Rust 后端、Flutter Web UI 和 SQLite，支持 Git LFS、SSH/HTTP Git 协议，以及兼容 GitLab 存储结构的迁移。
candidates.reuse: Rust backend, SQLite, SSH/HTTP/LFS and Flutter Web forge surface.
candidates.limitations: Root Cargo declares MIT but no license text found in inspected tree; provenance/notice text must be completed before vendoring. Flutter frontend and SQLite differ from gitr.

candidates.description: Fast, lightweight, open-source, self-hosted Github-compatible platform used for hosting source code, CI and managing software development projects.
candidates.reuse: GitHub-compatible forge REST models and Actions/matrix modules; reef-git manifest uses gix.
candidates.limitations: Source behavior not deeply inspected; complete GitHub compatibility not verified. Keep as second forge comparison after IronForge/Rbit.

candidates.description: [WIP] Self-hosted git server
candidates.reuse: Small Rust self-hosted server candidate.
candidates.limitations: WIP, last metadata push 2024; no deep module audit.

candidates.description: Small self-hosted git, written in rust
candidates.reuse: Minimal self-hosted Git frontend.
candidates.limitations: Older project; no deep module audit. Distinct from w4/rgit.

candidates.description: Dependency-free smart HTTP Git server for local testing aimed for production use
candidates.reuse: Small Smart HTTP server; useful local interop fixture candidate.
candidates.limitations: README-style dependency-free claim not source-audited; low priority beside opendata.

candidates.description: A basic lightweight git server to put on local networks.
candidates.reuse: Lightweight local-network Git server candidate.
candidates.limitations: No module inspection; limited product scope.

candidates.description: ❤️🪵 Radicle Heartwood Protocol & Stack (mirror)
candidates.reuse: Signed collaborative objects, issues/patches, identities, ref syntax validation, DAG and crypto crates.
candidates.limitations: Workspace includes vendored libgit2 and SQLite; decentralized collaborative merges do not supply gitr's linearizable mutable-ref authority. Select crates/contracts rather than whole node.

candidates.description: git over Freenet: decentralized git hosting on the Freenet network
candidates.reuse: Remote helper, signed identity, repository/pack contracts and encoding types.
candidates.limitations: Freenet runtime/protocol coupling; not Iroh. Full Git semantic compatibility not independently validated.

candidates.description: Decentralized git node — self-hostable, Ed25519 identity, HTTP signatures, libp2p gossip. MIT/Apache-2.0.
candidates.reuse: GitLawb remote helper, Ed25519 attestation and libp2p node identity/authentication patterns.
candidates.limitations: Network and trust model differ from gitr. GitHub API NOASSERTION corrected by workspace manifest and license files; no runtime audit.

candidates.reuse: Stateless Git object-store server; manifest/WAL CAS and S3/GCS storage protocol reference.
candidates.limitations: Alternative authority design rather than a redb drop-in. Validate crash/CAS behavior under gitr invariants before borrowing.

candidates.description: Stateless git storage on an object store: many small repositories, no database, no leader — the bucket is the repository
candidates.reuse: Documented walgit fork, small-repository platform focus and versioned WAL modules.
candidates.limitations: Detached derivative verified by README, not solely GitHub fork flag. Preserve ancestor notices; compare specific modules before replacing upstream.

candidates.description: walgit fork: agent-collaborative development lab - a git server that is one binary in front of an object store
candidates.reuse: Documented walgit derivative with signed D1 collaboration/CI objects, Rust aggregation and protocol specification.
candidates.limitations: Includes Zig wg client/MCP and TypeScript SDK. Protocol ambitions do not prove distributed correctness or make whole codebase Rust.

candidates.description: Run a stateless Git server as a single binary over S3 or GCS, with smart HTTP, LFS, web UI, and webhooks.
candidates.reuse: Discovered detached similarly named copy; no demonstrated improvement over origin.
candidates.limitations: README directs install to unusually placed Software-premold.zip; no archive downloaded/executed. Prefer canonical origin; not asserting malware.

candidates.description: A modern, extensible, high-performance CI/CD engine written in Rust.
candidates.reuse: petgraph DAG validation, matrix expansion, pipeline specification and Extism plugin contracts.
candidates.limitations: Early alpha; active runs and queued work in scheduler are in-memory Arc/RwLock structures. Full deployment PostgreSQL/NATS. Use pure modules, not durability authority.

candidates.description: Programmable CI/CD engine without Containers, written in Rust, built on top of Wasm and Nix ❄️
candidates.reuse: Workflow task policies, retry/success/failure/always behavior, outputs/artifacts and Wasm extension contract.
candidates.limitations: Wasm orchestrates host commands/Nix/pkgx tools; a Wasm plugin alone does not isolate its host subprocess actions. MPL duties apply to reused files.

candidates.description: Durable & Deterministic Workflow Runtime
candidates.reuse: Replay/event-log semantics, storage ExecutionLog/Version contracts, retries and execution ownership.
candidates.limitations: Pre-release; Wasmtime plus SQLite/PostgreSQL differ from selected Wasmi/redb. Suitable design/source donor under compatible licensing, not mandated runtime replacement.

candidates.description: Homestar is the individual node that makes up the Everywhere Computer network (similar to how IPFS Kubo, Iroh, Nabu, or other implementation nodes make up the IPFS network). It's written in Rust and is designed for performance and composability.
candidates.reuse: Content-addressed workflow/invocation/receipt schemas and DAG boundaries.
candidates.limitations: Last observed push 2024-09-26; Wasmtime, SQLite and libp2p. Inspect dependency freshness; use schemas/concepts selectively.

candidates.description: Programmable Continuous Integration system with WebAssembly runtime.

candidates.description: A build system and monorepo management tool for the web ecosystem, written in Rust.

candidates.description: The GitButler version control client, backed by Git, powered by Tauri/Rust/Svelte
